properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION (b), AND NARROWER THAN (b) WAS WRITTEN.**

HIS WORDS: *"for the pages, I'd like to only use renderings of systems engineering views the agent generates from graph content of reflow2 itself. I'd like to have some cutting edge rendering (that we periodically update) to show that contents come from the graph and that with a good agent, you can create some pretty awesome views."*

⇒ **ONLY renderings. Not "mostly", not "landing page plus renderings" — (a) and (c) are both declined.** The page is a DEMONSTRATION, and its subject is its own provenance: it exists to show that the content came out of the graph and that a capable agent can render it well.

⭐⭐ **THAT PURPOSE SETS A HARDER HONESTY STANDARD THAN DOCUMENTATION, and it is the reason this is worth stating rather than just building.** A doc that drifts is stale. **A page whose entire claim is "this came from the graph" is FALSIFIED by one hand-written fact.** So `render_views.py`'s existing doctrine is not a nicety here, it is the product: *"it may only emit what the graph states… anything a viewpoint NEEDS but the graph cannot supply goes on the CONFESSIONS list."* The confessions are not a blemish on the demo — **they are the strongest evidence the rest is real.**

⚠️ **THE COST HE ACCEPTED, STATED PLAINLY: A NEWCOMER LANDS ON SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING VIEWS WITH NO ORIENTATION.** "Only renderings" means the page cannot carry a hand-written *"reflow2 is a persistent design brain…"* paragraph. Someone arriving cold meets a functional view before they know what they are looking at. **His own next sentence is plausibly the answer to this — see `dec:idea-a-generated-explainer-for-someone-new` — and that connection is recorded rather than assumed.**

⚠️ **"PERIODICALLY UPDATE" CARRIES A KNOWN COST, ALREADY MEASURED HERE.** `chg:impact-propagation-is-rendered-not-written`: a re-render churns wording, so the diff is noisy and *"drift here will need reading as 're-rendered', not as 'the design moved'"*. A page refreshed on a schedule will do this every time. Worth deciding once whether the refresh is committed output (noisy diffs, reviewable) or an Actions deploy that never commits (clean repo, unreviewable) — which is the placement question below, now materially easier because **nothing on the page is hand-written, so nothing is lost by not committing it.**

═══ WHAT STAYS OPEN, DELIBERATELY ═══

· **WHICH views.** `docs/viewpoints.md` holds the catalogue and `render_views.py` renders several; which of them belong on a public page, and in what order, is unanswered.
· **WHAT "cutting edge rendering" means.** He asked for it and did not specify. Not inferred.
· **PLACEMENT.** `index.html` at the repo root was his sketch, prefaced *"something like this"*. This root is a Rust workspace; `/docs` already exists and already holds `loop-dag.html`; an Actions deploy commits nothing. **The ruling above makes the Actions route cheaper than it was**, but it is not chosen here.
· **REFRESH CADENCE.** "Periodically" is not a schedule.

📌 STILL NOT ASKED AND STILL NOT ASSUMED: whether this is reflow2's own design published, or a template a CONSUMER could use for theirs. His wording — *"from graph content of reflow2 itself"* — answers it for THIS page and says nothing about the general case.

════════ THE OPTIONS AS PUT TO HIM, KEPT ════════

**(a) A LANDING PAGE** — hand-written, an afternoon, and every other tool has one. **DECLINED.** It goes stale the way `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, and this project has been bitten: a doc presented eight impact kinds never implemented and referenced an edge type retired five days before it was written.

**(b) ⭐ THE DESIGN GRAPH, RENDERED — CHOSEN**, and narrowed to *only* this.

**(c) BOTH, LAYERED** — **DECLINED**, which also declines the shape `dec:idea-which-docs-can-never-be-a-projection` is open about. ⚠️ That decision stays open for the rest of reflow2's outward docs; this ruling covers the PAGE only, and does not settle it generally.

REAFFIRMED 2026-09-28 by Anthony. Asked whether the documentation site (dec:idea-the-repo-front-door-is-minimal-and-the-documentation-is-a-small-site) could be a few hand-written HTML pages instead, he chose: "Keep: pages generated from graph". So the site that replaces docs/ carries renderings of reflow2's own design, in flo2.io's layout, and this decision governs it unchanged.
properties.name: DECIDED — the public page carries ONLY renderings the agent generates from reflow2's own graph; the page is the evidence for its own claim
properties.rationale:
Captured under capture-intent rather than built, because he sequenced it explicitly ("post release") and because the one thing that decides the size of the work — what is on the page — is the one thing he did not say.

The mechanism he described is recorded as a SKETCH rather than a specification, on his own framing of "something like this". Transcribing `index.html` at the root into a requirement would have converted an illustration into a commitment, in a repository whose root is a cargo workspace.

Recorded as its own node rather than folded into the requirement because it reaches two decisions that were already open before he asked — outward docs as projections, and which docs can never be one — and a question connecting three threads deserves to be findable from all of them. The near-duplicate guard fired on the requirement and was right to: they are the same subject, and saying so on the record is cheaper than a reader later wondering whether one supersedes the other.
